laws.rule: Foreign tourists who enter Baja California Sur and stay more than 24 hours owe a state charge (an aprovechamiento) for the use of state infrastructure and services. The law sets it at MXN 350 (about A$26.45), updated each 1 January in line with the consumer price index, and the state finance department (Secretaría de Finanzas y Administración) sets how it's collected through general rules (Ley de Hacienda del Estado, art. 129 Bis).

Los Cabos municipality (Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo) charges an environmental sanitation fee: 70% of the daily UMA, about MXN 82.12 (about A$6.21), per room occupied in a hotel, inn, hostel or motel; 2 UMA, about MXN 234.62 (about A$17.73), per room, house or apartment booked through a digital platform; 10% of the daily UMA, about MXN 11.73 (about A$0.89), on bar and restaurant bills over 4 UMA, about MXN 469.24 (about A$35.46), shown on the receipt (not for hotel guests eating in the same hotel's outlets); and 50% of the daily UMA, about MXN 58.66 (about A$4.43), per day of car hire and per rental of a recreational or sports boat (Ley de Hacienda para el Municipio de Los Cabos, art. 137 Bis to 137 Octies).

Balandra protected area (La Paz): CONANP's visitor rules say take your rubbish, use authorised trails only, don't climb the dune or the mushroom rock, take care near the sinkhole, keep dogs on a lead on the main beach, and use the dry toilets (relieving yourself anywhere else isn't allowed).

local-law.notes: Amounts use the 2026 UMA (Unidad de Medida y Actualización, a federal reference unit: MXN 117.31 a day from 1 February 2026, INEGI) and A$1 = about MXN 13.23 (RBA 30 October 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040; Banco de México FIX for 30 October 2026, USD 1 = MXN 18.7962). The 2026 indexed amount of the state charge and its collection rules weren't found; check with the state finance department. Other municipalities (La Paz, Loreto, Comondú, Mulegé) aren't checked here.

layers.authority: CONANP (Comision Nacional de Areas Naturales Protegidas), Parque Nacional Cabo Pulmo
layers.process: Entry fee of MXN 125 per person per day (about A$9.45; A$1 = about MXN 13.23 (RBA 30 October 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040; Banco de Mexico FIX, USD 1 = MXN 18.7962)). Exempt: older adults, pensioners and retirees, people with disability and children under 12 (credential shown on entry). 75% off for students and teachers with a credential; 50% off for Mexican nationals and foreign residents who show an official document. Open 8:00 to 18:00 daily. Visitors use service providers that hold the required authorisation.

layers.process: Entry fee of MXN 125 per person per day (about A$9.45; A$1 = about MXN 13.23 (RBA 30 October 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040; Banco de Mexico FIX, USD 1 = MXN 18.7962)). Exempt: older adults, pensioners and retirees, people with disability and children under 12 (credential shown on entry). 75% off for students and teachers with a credential; 50% off for Mexican nationals and foreign residents who show an official document. Open two shifts, 8:00 to 12:00 and 13:00 to 17:00; the digital passes are for the second shift. Capped at 450 people per shift.
